correctness.rationale: For vertices, two omitted indices leave their same-shore vertices indistinguishable, and a chosen landmark distinguishes either endpoint of its own index from every other index. For edges a coordinate equals 1 away from both endpoint indices, 0 at a chosen endpoint and 2 at a chosen opposite vertex of an endpoint index. This decodes the side and location of the detected endpoints and recovers a missing endpoint at the sole omitted index. Conversely if i,j are omitted, the edges a_i b_t and a_j b_t for a third index t are indistinguishable. Thus the minimum basis family is the same for both metrics. A slide necessarily sends a token to the unique vacant index and flips its side; every such move is legal. With m=n-1, length equals m+2d for d decreasing moves. The initial b₀ must be removed, and an a₀ must be separately installed before the last move removes it to finish on the B shore. These are two separate decreases. With exactly two, the initial strictly increasing excursion visits distinct nonzero indices and is closed by the first decrease removing b₀. The next move must place a₀: otherwise b₀ is reinstalled and would require another decrease. If the excursion visits t+1 nonzero indices, it leaves t B landmarks; 1≤t≤m-1 is necessary and sufficient. The second decrease can use any one of those t B landmarks. Thereafter only increasing moves are possible: the remaining m-t A landmarks at nonzero indices can be visited in any order, followed by the forced slide from 0. This yields (m)_(t+1)·t·(m-t)!=m!t(m-t) distinct labelled paths and realizes the lower bound m+4. The sum is m!·m(m-1)(m+1)/6=(n-1)! binom(n,3). In particular n=3 allows t=1 and gives two length-six paths. Inspected artifacts/verify_original.py, artifacts/verify_quotient.py and recorded verification_output.txt without replay: they supply respectively direct finite BFS for n=3..7 and weighted orbit BFS for n=3..100, not the proof for all n.
